newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD to launch Level 3 ADR in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD to launch Level 3 ADR in 1997.

text.p: Brazil's state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) plans to launch Level 3 American Depositary Receipts (ADR) next year in connection with its privatization, a company official said.

"We are not planning to issue new shares," said CVRD market relations spokesman Antonio Maria de Castro Pereira. "The Level 3 ADR will represent those shares which are being included in the global offering."

CVRD's privatization is due to kick off in February or March next year with an initial block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares. Immediately after the block sale, 5.11 percent of CVRD's capital stock will be offered to employees, followed by a global public offering of the remaining shares held by the government.
The government owns 76 percent of CVRD's voting capital, equivalent to 51 percent of the company's total capital.
Pereira said a listing on the New York stock Exchange via a Level 3 ADR would facilitate the sale of the global offer shares in other financial markets around the world.
He said CVRD had registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in December 1994 in order to be in a position to launch a Level 2 or 3 ADR.
"The government will decide when to launch the Level Three ADR," Pereira said. "It is advisable to launch the ADR at least four months prior to the global offer."
CVRD already has a Level One New York ADR listing.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
